# Brief for the coach: the Monday incline curl

## What was looked at

I compared the old program (the July-to-October plan with its Week A / Week B rotation) against the program now in force, exercise by exercise. The old plan had direct biceps work on two days of every week: incline curls plus hammer curls on one pull day and incline curls on another, alongside ordinary dumbbell curls. The current program has direct biceps work on one day only: Sunday's deadlift session, with Bicep Curl (Dumbbell) for 3 sets of 8–12 reps at an effort of 8 out of 10, and Hammer Curl (Dumbbell) for 3 sets of 10–12 at the same effort. That is 6 direct sets a week, all in one session, against a program target of 10 hard sets per muscle per week. Biceps do get secondary work from the band pull-ups, negatives and rows, and the Tuesday chest-and-back session with the trainer is estimated at 3 biceps sets, but the direct work was thin.

Joe's profile says direct biceps work is dumbbell curls, not barbell, which the old program's incline curl fits.

## The change, now recorded

I added **Incline Curl (Dumbbell)** as the last exercise of the Monday session (overhead press, back and arms):

- 3 sets of 8–12 reps, effort 8 out of 10
- 75 seconds rest between sets
- Progression: double progression, meaning the weight goes up once every set reaches 12 reps
- Cues: bench at about 45 degrees, arms hanging straight down behind the torso, elbows staying back with a full stretch at the bottom, no swinging from the shoulder

Direct biceps work goes from 6 sets in one session to 9 sets across two days, and the incline curl trains the muscle at a long length, which the Sunday curls don't.

No starting weight was written down for the incline curl, so the first Monday's load needs to be chosen. The engine will fill it from history if Joe has logged incline curls before; if it comes up empty, pick something Joe can take to 12 reps at a genuine 8 out of 10 and let the double progression carry it from there.

This is now the fourth version of the program, recorded as an amendment (not a redesign) on 4 Nov 2026. Nothing else moved: the rotation stays at Week A, and the training block that opened on 1 Nov 2026 continues without a reset. The reason recorded against the version reads: direct biceps work was six sets in one session; an incline curl on Monday makes it nine over two days, at long muscle length, and keeps the lightest lifting day inside its cap.

Time check for Monday: the estimate with the new exercise is 53 minutes against a 75-minute cap, so it stays well inside. For reference, the other sessions estimate at Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90.

Before recording, the engine checked Hevy for anything new between 20:40 and 20:53 on 4 Nov 2026 and found no new workouts, weigh-ins or routine edits.

## What Joe needs to agree to

The change is in the engine's records but **not yet in Hevy**. Hevy only gets written when the next week's plan is drafted and pushed, and that push asks for approval first. So before Monday's routine in Hevy shows the incline curl, Joe needs to:

1. Agree that Monday grows by one exercise (three sets, roughly five extra minutes).
2. Approve the next weekly plan push, which is also the step that resolves the Hevy drift below.

If Joe would rather not, nothing further happens: Hevy stays as it is and the next plan can be drafted without the line.

## Warnings, and what each one means

Five warnings came back. Two were already standing and have written reasons attached; three are about Hevy.

**Three routines in Hevy don't match the plan approved on 2 Nov 2026.** Joe has edited numbers in Hevy since the plan was pushed:

- In one routine, the second set's duration on the first exercise differs.
- In a second, the reps on sets 5, 6 and 7 of the first exercise differ, and the weights on sets 1, 2 and 3 of the second exercise differ.
- In a third, the weights on sets 1 through 4 of the third exercise differ, the durations on sets 1 and 2 of the fourth exercise differ, and the weights on sets 1 through 3 of the sixth exercise differ.

For training this changes nothing: Joe lifts what is in Hevy and logs it. It is the engine saying Hevy and the plan disagree. It clears one of two ways: either the next weekly plan writes Joe's edits in as overrides (the plan accepts his numbers), or the next push rewrites those routines from the plan (the plan overwrites his numbers). Worth asking Joe which edits were deliberate before the next push, so the right one happens.

**Deadlift target is below the band.** The program targets 4 hard deadlift sets a week; the rule for a maintenance phase expects 5–15. This was left standing with a reason: Sunday plans exactly 4 hard sets (one top set of 5 at effort 8, then 3 back-off sets of 5), Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the hinge pattern, and the trainer sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday. A target of 5 would flag under-target every week the session was done as written. It clears only if the target is raised to 5 or more and the session changes to match. No action needed; it carries forward with the new version.

**The strict pull-up test doesn't fit a hypertrophy program.** Friday's first line is a single strict pull-up at maximum effort, held constant with no progression scheme, which the engine flags as off-emphasis. Also left standing with a reason: it is the weekly measure while Joe's max is 1. The negatives (3 sets of 2–4) and band pull-ups (4 sets of 5–8 on Wednesday, 3 sets of 5–8 on Sunday) do the building under their own progression, and the strict line becomes real working sets once the test rep passes about five. It clears when that happens and the line gets a scheme, or if the test is removed.

Both standing reasons were carried into the new version's record, so neither needs re-justifying.

## Other gaps from the comparison, not acted on

For your judgement, these exercises from the old program have no counterpart in the current one: lunges, single-leg Romanian deadlift, chest fly, assisted dips (replaced by dip negatives), assisted and inverted rows, straight-arm band pulldown, hollow and arch holds, hanging leg raise, side plank, seated calf raise, and the step-up and push-up from the old circuit. I did not add any of them; only the biceps gap matched something Joe has stated he wants.

Done. Incline curls are now the last exercise on Monday: 3 sets of 8 to 12 at an effort of 8, 75 seconds rest, with the weight going up once every set hits 12. Monday estimates at 53 of its 75 minutes, so it stays your lightest lifting day. Nothing else in the week moved and the block carries on as it was.

One thing to know: your Monday routine in Hevy won't show the incline curl until next week's plan is drafted and pushed, which you'll approve before anything changes. For the first session, if your history gives a sensible starting weight I'll use it; otherwise pick something you can take to 12 reps at a genuine 8 out of 10 and let the progression carry it.

**The deadlift dose**

The program sets a target of 4 hard deadlift sets a week. For a maintenance phase the general rule expects somewhere between 5 and 15, so the program sits just under the floor. I left it there on purpose, with the reason written down:

- Sunday plans exactly 4 hard sets: one top set of 5 at an effort of 8, then 3 back-off sets of 5.
- Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the hinge pattern through the rest of the week.
- Your trainer sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday.

If I set the target to 5, you'd come up short every single week you did Sunday exactly as written, which would be noise rather than information. It would only change if we raised the target to 5 or more and added a set to Sunday. Right now I don't think the deadlift needs more; the hinge is well covered. If you ever want to push it, say so and I'll adjust Sunday.

Separately: you've edited numbers in three of your Hevy routines since the plan went in on 2 November (some weights, some reps, a couple of durations). Before next week's push I need to know which of those were deliberate, so the plan keeps them rather than overwriting them. Tell me when convenient and I'll carry them forward.
